positions.subject: q:government/expand-mayoral-authority
positions.summary: Says he will vote no on the Mayor's charter amendments because they concentrate too much power in the Mayor's Office, and that he does not believe any mayor should get more authority to hire and fire department heads and commissioners.

citations.quote: I will be voting no on the Mayor's Clean Up City Hall charter amendments because I believe they concentrate too much power in the Mayor's Office and make it harder for everyday San Franciscans to have a voice in their government.
citations.locator: p. 12, answer to "How will you vote on the Mayor's Clean Up City Hall ballot measures on the November ballot?"

citations.quote: I support making City Hall work better, but I don't believe the answer is giving any mayor more authority to hire and fire department heads and commissioners with less independent oversight.
citations.locator: p. 12, answer to "How will you vote on the Mayor's Clean Up City Hall ballot measures on the November ballot?"

positions.subject: q:housing/citywide-rezoning
positions.summary: Says he would not have supported the Mayor's Family Zoning Plan as written because it did not protect two-unit buildings, many of them rent-controlled; says he supports building more housing and focusing new housing along commercial corridors.

citations.quote: For that reason, I would not have supported Mayor Lurie's Family Zoning Plan as written. While I support building more homes, I was concerned that the plan did not protect two-unit buildings.
citations.locator: p. 11, answer to "How did you vote or would you have voted on Mayor Lurie’s Family Zoning Plan?"

citations.quote: I support focusing new housing along commercial corridors, where it can strengthen neighborhood business districts and make better use of existing infrastructure.
citations.locator: p. 11, answer to "How did you vote or would you have voted on Mayor Lurie’s Family Zoning Plan?"

positions.subject: q:housing/expand-rent-control
positions.summary: Says San Francisco should strengthen and expand rent control where legally possible.

citations.quote: We should also strengthen and expand rent control where legally possible.
citations.locator: p. 13, answer to "How would you address affordability in your District?"

citations.quote: That means investing in permanently affordable housing, protecting and expanding rent control where legally possible,
citations.locator: p. 11, answer to "How did you vote or would you have voted on Mayor Lurie’s Family Zoning Plan?"
